source.title: Machine Learning and Non-Invasive Monitoring Technologies for Training Load Management in Women’s Volleyball: A Scoping Review

paper.citation: Sanhueza Tapia H.G., Giakoni-Ramírez F., De Souza-Lima J., Diaz Suarez A. Machine Learning and Non-Invasive Monitoring Technologies for Training Load Management in Women’s Volleyball: A Scoping Review. Sports. 2026;14(2):74. doi:10.3390/sports14020074.
paper.abstract: This paper addresses the following question: What non-invasive monitoring and AI/ML approaches have been used for load, fatigue, performance, and injury-related outcomes in women’s volleyball? Female volleyball players at any level, plus mixed-sex studies with at least 35% female participants. Evidence published from January 2020 through September 2025. JBI-guided scoping review reported with PRISMA-ScR. Searched Scopus, Web of Science, and PubMed.
paper.tldr: Fifty-three sources were included: 48 primary studies and five secondary syntheses. IMUs, force plates, heart-rate/HRV measures, wellness questionnaires, and positioning systems were common; ML applications were less frequent. Use the review to choose candidate signals, then validate them locally.
paper.methods: JBI-guided scoping review reported with PRISMA-ScR. Searched Scopus, Web of Science, and PubMed. Narrative/thematic evidence mapping without formal risk-of-bias appraisal.
paper.findings: Fifty-three sources were included: 48 primary studies and five secondary syntheses. IMUs, force plates, heart-rate/HRV measures, wellness questionnaires, and positioning systems were common; ML applications were less frequent. External-load intensity indicators were reported more often as fatigue-sensitive than accumulated volume, but heterogeneous definitions prevent a universal metric hierarchy. Female biological moderators, including menstrual-cycle context, were rarely addressed.
paper.limitations: No formal quality appraisal was performed, so this is an evidence map rather than an effectiveness ranking. Language and full-text restrictions may have excluded studies. Methods, technologies, metrics, and outcomes were highly heterogeneous. Volleyball findings do not automatically transfer to football movement or contact demands.
paper.practicalImplications: Use the review to choose candidate signals, then validate them locally. Favor interpretable measures tied to a decision and resist deploying ML until labels, missingness, external validation, and female-specific context are explicit.
paper.athleteDev: For athlete development, use the review to choose candidate signals, then validate them locally. Favor interpretable measures tied to a decision and resist deploying ML until labels, missingness, external validation, and female-specific context are explicit. Apply the finding within the population and setting described in the source rather than treating it as a universal threshold.
paper.rtp: The paper did not validate a rehabilitation or return-to-sport decision rule. Its findings may inform supporting training or monitoring during reconditioning, but it provides no standalone clearance threshold or progression criterion.
